revisions.title: Separating form, becoming, and space
revisions.body: Here Timaeus separates three roles that are easy to collapse. The visible things are generated likenesses; the receptacle is the invisible, formless receiver in which they appear. His images of gold beneath changing shapes, and of mother and nurse, help mark that distinction without turning the receptacle into an element. By 52a-d he names the three as form, generated likeness, and space. The last is not presented as ordinary sense knowledge: it is reached by a difficult, barely credible kind of reasoning.
